title: ECR: publish an artifact you can identify and replace
outcome: Explain image tags, digests, registry access, scan results, and release retention.

trace.title: Source revision
trace.detail:
## Understand the idea

A container registry stores images. A tag is a name that can move unless policy prevents it.

A digest identifies image content. Deploying latest makes it difficult to know what actually ran during an incident.

ECR integrates registry access with AWS identity. Build/push identity and workload pull identity can have different permissions.

A successful push does not prove the image runs, and a vulnerability scan does not prove the application is safe or compatible.

Setup: create a deliberate training repository, configure tag policy/retention, authenticate the build identity, build from an identified source revision, push a revision tag, record the digest, and test pull/run under the workload’s identity.

Keep rollback artifacts long enough for the release plan.

trace.title: Follow one item
trace.detail:
Build → scan/check → push → resolve digest → deploy that artifact → observe → roll back to a known digest if needed. Connect logs/deployment metadata to the source and digest.

Retention rules must not remove every artifact needed for rollback. Large layers and old tags also consume storage; define a deliberate policy.

trace.title: Try the failure
trace.detail: latest can mean different images on two machines. Credentials copied into a Docker layer remain in the image even if a later command removes the file.
